title: Transactional Groundwater Exchange Two-Phase Commit Readiness Remediation
trigger: F-GC21 pre-implementation atomicity audit found that two sequential component commits are not formally atomic while the groundwater commit_backend remains recoverably fallible after all orchestrator acceptance checks.
problem: If SWAP commits and the groundwater backend subsequently rejects commit, or groundwater commits and SWAP subsequently rejects commit, the coupled window can become half-committed. That is incompatible with transactional time-step semantics and hard coupled mass conservation.
objective: Strengthen the F-GC18 service with an opt-in preparable subtype. A groundwater candidate may first enter a reversible prepared/reserved state. Once prepared, final groundwater publication has no recoverable rejection path. GC21 can then prepare groundwater, attempt the fully prevalidated SWAP commit, abort groundwater preparation if SWAP refuses, and perform deterministic groundwater publication only after SWAP succeeds.
required_semantics: retain the existing F-GC18 base service ABI and behavior
add an opt-in preparable service subtype rather than forcing all groundwater services to support two-phase commit
prepare validates checkpoint/candidate provenance and creates one opaque prepared handle
prepared state remains reversible until final publication
abort prepared leaves committed groundwater state unchanged
final commit of a valid prepared handle has no recoverable status return and therefore cannot be refused as a normal runtime outcome
no coupled orchestration is implemented in this remediation
no external-model-specific API, file or calendar assumption
qualification: existing F-GC18 lifecycle tests remain green
prepare then abort leaves committed state unchanged
prepare then commit publishes exactly once
duplicate prepare/commit misuse fails closed before publication
stale or mismatched candidate cannot prepare
hard_nonclaims: no distributed transaction protocol over files or networks
no claim that process crashes are recoverable without later restart work
